text: In the days when the judges ruled, a famine struck the land, and a man from Bethlehem in Judah went to live in the country of Moab, taking his wife and two sons with him.

The man's name was Elimelech, his wife's name was Naomi, and their two sons were named Mahlon and Chilion; they were Ephrathites from Bethlehem in Judah. They arrived in the fields of Moab and settled there.
Then Elimelech, Naomi's husband, died, leaving her alone with her two sons.
The sons married Moabite women, one named Orpah and the other Ruth, and the family lived there about ten years.
Then both Mahlon and Chilion also died, leaving Naomi without her husband or either of her two sons.
When Naomi heard in Moab that the LORD had visited his people and given them food again, she set out with her daughters-in-law to return home from the country of Moab.
She left the place where she had been living, and her two daughters-in-law went with her, walking the road that would take them back to the land of Judah.
But Naomi said to her two daughters-in-law, Go back, each of you, to your mother's home. May the LORD show you the same kindness you showed to your husbands who died, and to me.
May the LORD grant that each of you find rest in the home of a new husband. Then she kissed them, and they wept aloud.
They said to her, No, we will go back with you to your people.
But Naomi said, Turn back, my daughters. Why would you come with me? Do I have any more sons in my womb who could become husbands for you?
Turn back, my daughters, and go on your way, for I am too old to have another husband. Even if I said there was hope for me tonight, and I bore sons,
would you wait for them to grow up? Would you refuse to marry for their sake? No, my daughters. My life is far more bitter than yours, because the LORD's hand has turned against me.
Then they wept aloud again, and Orpah kissed her mother-in-law and said goodbye, but Ruth clung to her and would not let go.
Naomi said, Look, your sister-in-law has gone back to her people and her gods. Go back with her.
But Ruth answered, Do not urge me to leave you or turn back from following you. Where you go I will go, and where you stay I will stay. Your people will be my people, and your God will be my God.
Where you die I will die, and there I will be buried. May the LORD punish me, even severely, if anything but death separates you and me.
When Naomi saw that Ruth was determined to go with her, she stopped urging her.
So the two women went on together until they came to Bethlehem. When they arrived, the whole town was stirred, and the women asked, Can this be Naomi?
She told them, Do not call me Naomi; call me Mara, for the Almighty has made my life very bitter.
I went away full, but the LORD has brought me back empty. Why call me Naomi, when the LORD has spoken against me and brought hardship upon me?
So Naomi returned from the country of Moab with her daughter-in-law Ruth the Moabite, and they arrived in Bethlehem just as the barley harvest was beginning.
